pairs: Respondens autem Job dixit:
Then Job responded by saying:
Cujus adjutor es?
Whose assistant are you?
numquid imbecillis?
Is he weak-minded?
et sustentas brachium ejus qui non est fortis?
And do you sustain the arm of him that is not strong?
Cui dedisti consilium?
To whom have you given advice?
forsitan illi qui non habet sapientiam:
Perhaps it is to him that has no wisdom
et prudentiam tuam ostendisti plurimam.
or prudence that you have revealed your many ideas.
Quem docere voluisti?
Who is it that you wanted to teach?
nonne eum qui fecit spiramentum?
Was it not him that created the breath of life?
Ecce gigantes gemunt sub aquis,
Behold, giant things groan under the waters,
et qui habitant cum eis.
and they dwell with them.
Nudus est infernus coram illo,
The underworld is naked before him,
et nullum est operimentum perditioni.
and there is no covering for perdition.
Qui extendit aquilonem super vacuum,
He stretched out the North over emptiness,
et appendit terram super nihilum.
and he suspended the land over nothing.
Qui ligat aquas in nubibus suis,
He secures the waters in his clouds,
ut non erumpant pariter deorsum.
so that they do not burst forth downward all at once.
Qui tenet vultum solii sui,
He holds back the face of his throne,
et expandit super illud nebulam suam.
and he stretches his cloud over it.
Terminum circumdedit aquis,
He has set limits around the waters,
usque dum finiantur lux et tenebræ.
until light and darkness shall reach their limit.
Columnæ cæli contremiscunt,
The pillars of heaven tremble
et pavent ad nutum ejus.
and are frightened at his nod.
In fortitudine illius repente maria congregata sunt,
By his strength, the seas suddenly gather together,
et prudentia ejus percussit superbum.
and his foresight has struck the arrogant.
Spiritus ejus ornavit cælos,
His spirit has adorned the heavens,
et obstetricante manu ejus, eductus est coluber tortuosus.
and his birthing hand has brought forth the winding serpent.
Ecce hæc ex parte dicta sunt viarum ejus:
Behold, these things have been said about his ways in part,
et cum vix parvam stillam sermonis ejus audierimus,
and, since we barely have heard a small drop of his word,
quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis illius intueri?
who will be able to gaze upon the thunder of his greatness?
